title: Potain topless tower cranes power landmark healthcare developments in Jakarta
summary: Potain MCT 205 and MCT 325 were configured for efficient multi-crane operations.Topless design optimizes overlap and site utilization in dense city environments.
body_markdown:
- Potain MCT 205 and MCT 325 were configured for efficient multi-crane operations.
- Topless design optimizes overlap and site utilization in dense city environments.


Topless tower cranes from Potain played a key role in the construction of two major healthcare facilities in Jakarta, Indonesia: the National Cardiovascular Centre Harapan Kita and Dharmais Cancer Hospital. A Potain[MCT 205](https://www.manitowoc.com/potain/top-slewing-cranes-asia/mct-205) worked at the Dharmais site, while a Potain[MCT 325 L16](https://www.manitowoc.com/potain/top-slewing-cranes-asia/mct-325-l16) supported work at RS Harapan Kita. The cranes were rented to the projects by[PT Potaindo Machinery](https://potaindo.com/) , which also provided responsive support to both cranes via its experienced technician teams and strong parts availability. The main contractor on both jobs was PP-Wika KSO, a joint venture between[PT PP (Persero) Tbk](https://www.ptpp.co.id/en) and PT Wijaya Karya (Persero) Tbk.


The cranes are well-suited to local requirements, delivering the right balance of lifting performance and efficiency. Their topless design also enabled them to efficiently coordinate with other tower cranes on the projects, with manageable overlap helping optimise operations and maintain productivity.


Working in a dense urban hospital environment presented additional challenges, requiring careful planning of crane placement. Both cranes were installed at the edges of the sites, adjacent to surrounding roads, to maximise available working space. The cranes were primarily handling structural steel and concrete.


The Potain MCT 325 L16 at RS Harapan Kita was configured with a 55 m jib and a hook height of 112 m, delivering a tip load of 5.1 t. This setup provided the reach and lifting performance to support construction across the site without the need for additional modifications or optional features.


Despite the challenges typical of complex urban projects, the cranes delivered reliable performance throughout the build. Operations remained on track, supporting steady progress toward completion at the end of April 2026.


“Projects such as the National Heart Center and Dharmais Cancer Hospital show how Potain topless cranes deliver the flexibility and precision required for complex urban construction. The MCT 205 and MCT 325 L16 offer the right balance of performance and ease of operation, helping contractors meet demanding timelines while working within restricted site conditions,” said Johnny Kuah, regional sales manager, Potain.
